_numbering_note: catalog_number pending the base/hybrid renumbering (see gdd-culture-emergence-and-territory.md); csv_id is the authoritative key for now.
sub_palette: germanic (gothic) backbone + near_eastern (akkadian) overlay (cross-family blend, Germanic-leaning)

blend.backbone: germanic (continental / Gothic register: thiudans/reiks, dithematic -s/-az names, retained th/w, ai/au diphthongs, heavy root-initial stress)
blend.overlay: near_eastern (akkadian: the alu/bit river-cities, the sangu temple-priesthood, construct-chain toponyms, emphatic gutturals, SOV agglutinative grammar)
blend.lean: Germanic-heavy - a Germanic war-aristocracy (a thiudans-house) enthroned over the Akkadian temple-cities of the Two Rivers: the war-band rules, the scribal-priestly city endures and serves beneath.

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_01 Thiodmark (Germanic) x BASE_03 Shinarur (Mesopotamian). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Germanic base = Clanhold, Mesopotamian base = Civilized, and any Civ parent -> Civ, so Ashurheim is Civilized (feudal). Concept: a Germanic war-host that conquered the river-valley city-states of the Two Rivers and set up as kings over the temple-cities (an Assyrian-Germanic fusion; 'Ashur's-home'). Backbone = Germanic (Gothic/continental: the ruling war-aristocracy, the thiudans/reiks register, dithematic names); overlay/substrate = Akkadian (the alu-cities, the bit-ili temples, the scribal populace, the construct-chain toponyms). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Gothic and Akkadian registers (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (Gothic reflexes primary, Akkadian variants secondary), never real gods. PROVISIONAL: alignment (Lawful/Neutral) is a per-hybrid design choice pending the alignment pass - the Germanic war-oath order meets the Akkadian law-stele tradition. Register choice: Germanic-base hybrids default to the GOTHIC/continental reflexes (Thiodmark = *theudo-mark, 'people-march'); Brythald (HYB_01) is the Anglo-Saxon special case - flag for Jedidiah if a uniform Germanic register is wanted instead. [UPDATE 2026-06-27: all human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic (per-hybrid alignment restriction removed). Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are now English (or an approved foreign term); conlang titles moved to ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue. Deities unchanged: canonical Agrippan pantheon via the per-family morph method.]

phonology.palette: Germanic (Gothic) backbone - heavy root-initial stress, sharp stops p/t/k b/d/g, retained th/w, ai/au diphthongs, dithematic compounding - meeting an Akkadian overlay: emphatic and guttural consonants (q, kh, h, ', sh, ts), triconsonantal roots, a/i/u vowels, -u/-um endings. Per the CSV: harsh gutturals mixed with sharp stops, heavy Germanic stress; grammar shifts toward SOV with agglutinative case-inflections (the Akkadian substrate) carried on Germanic strong/weak stems. Theophoric on the Gothic reflexes (Thulrs-, Erlands-) with Akkadian construct variants (Tullaru-, Urlandu-).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC; Germanic clusters (st, sk, br, kn) meeting Akkadian construct-chains and mimation -um; heavy initial stress with an Akkadian penultimate pull; dithematic Germanic names over Bit-/Dur-/Kar- construct toponyms.

sound_changes: Akkadian emphatics/gutturals -> Germanic inventory: q>k, emphatic-s>s, kh>h, glottal-stop>0
Akkadian case-vowels and mimation drop: final -u/-um/-tu>0 (or -tu>-th); roots become consonant-final
Gothic root-initial stress on all words; Gothic clusters (st, sk, br, kn) permitted
retain Gothic th, w, ai, au and Akkadian sh; very short roots take a Gothic -s/-a ending
fusion_rules.source_tilt: land/terrain/material/staple words from Akkadian roots (the substrate works the land); kin-line/quality/abstract/war words from Gothic roots (the ruling register); every root then filtered to one phonology

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Akkadian land-roots + Gothic rule/kin-roots, all run through one Germanic-shaped sound-law; portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Germanic ruling house keeps a dithematic lineage-name and -ingos; the Akkadian populace keep the 'mar-' (son of) patronymic and theophoric constructs; the throne fuses both - a thiudans who also carries a Bit- house-name.
morphology.compounding_rule: Germanic dithematic ([quality](stem) + element: Eisarna-burgs, iron-fort) layered over Akkadian construct-chains (Bit-[god], Dur-[ruler], Kar-[god]): the capital Ashur-heim (Ashur's-home), Dur-Theuda (fort of the Theuda-house).

title_ladder.government: feudal (a Germanic war-aristocracy over the Akkadian temple-cities: the thiudans and his reiks-kin at the crown, the kindins-governors over the alu-cities, the gardingus-retainers sworn to the war-host; the sangu-priesthood and the scribal ekallu serve beneath)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Gothic ladder, ascending, with the Akkadian substrate co-titles beneath. Gardingus (king's-man) barony; Marka-frauja (march-lord) march; Kindins (provincial governor) county; Drauhtins (war-lord; *druhtinaz) duchy; Reiks (prince-ruler) principality; Thiudans (king) kingdom over a Thiudangardi (Gothic 'kingdom'); Sharr-Thiudans (the king-of-kings; Akk sharru + Gmc thiudans) empire over the Kishsha-Thiudi (the 'totality of the people'). The conquered cities keep their Akkadian shaknu (governor) and sangu (priest) beneath the Germanic crown. The gudja (priest) and the scribal shatammu stand outside the ladder. Rank titles fuse the real Gothic and Akkadian registers (allowed).
title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH (or an approved commonly-known foreign term where set in 'ruler'). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: the Germanic ruling stock carry a dithematic name + -ingos lineage; the Akkadian populace carry a theophoric given name + mar- patronymic; order given-first.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the Germanic war-aristocracy keep Gothic dithematic names (Theud-, Erman-, -reiks, -mers); the Akkadian city-folk keep theophoric names (X-iddina, Warad-X) on the morphed canon-stems.
people_name_convention.theophoric: Germanic devotional on the Gothic god-reflexes (Thulris-mers, Erlands-); Akkadian devotional constructs: Warad-Tullaru (servant of Tullaru), Tullaru-iddina (Tullaru-gave-me).

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Gothic Germanic reflexes PRIMARY (family_germanic theonym_ancestors, the gothic column), Akkadian variants SECONDARY (the family_near_eastern / hammuran morphs), never real Germanic/Mesopotamian gods. Alignment PROVISIONAL (Lawful/Neutral): the Germanic war-oath order meets the Akkadian law-stele tradition.
religion.the_one: Aiterns (Gothic; Akk Itarnu) - the distant Ancient One, honored not petitioned

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Aiterns, Thulrs the just, Erlands of the sworn war, Riala the merciful - and names the Chaotic powers skohsla (demons), warded; the war-oath and the law-stele bind alike
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the ancestral war-dead (the Anses of the ruling house) and the city-spirits of the bit-ili; the great powers invoked at the alhs-grove and the temple situationally
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon, and names the Lawful powers - and Aiterns - as the tyrant-gods to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as skohsla (Gothic demons) or -lemnu (Akkadian evil), keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Marahs the War-Brand (Akk Marakshu the City-Burner); Vacidus -> Wakiths the Unmaker (Akk Bakidu-lemnu); Lusanto -> Lusanths the Hoard-Worm.
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Alhs (Germanic grove-temple) or Bit-ili (Akkadian god-house) of [power]: 'the Alhs of Thulrs', 'the Bit-ili of Tullaru'.
religion.saints_pattern: the Anses (the deified war-dead of the ruling house) and the deified law-givers of the cities, inscribed on the stele and honored at the howe and the ziggurat.
